bib.title: Janus: Decoupling Visual Encoding for Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation

question: Can one autoregressive transformer do both multimodal understanding and image generation without the conflict that arises when a single visual encoder serves both?
hypothesis: Understanding needs high-level semantic features while generation needs fine-grained spatial detail, so a single shared visual encoder forces a trade-off that hurts understanding; decoupling the encoders removes it.
contributions: Janus, an autoregressive framework with two independent visual encoding pathways feeding one unified transformer
Claims to be first to highlight the importance of decoupling visual encoding in unified understanding and generation
State-of-the-art among unified models of comparable size on understanding and generation benchmarks
Ablations showing decoupling matters and that unified training costs little versus task-specific training

method.summary: Janus uses SigLIP-Large-Patch16-384 for understanding and the LlamaGen VQ tokenizer for generation, each with a two-layer MLP adaptor, feeding one DeepSeek-LLM 1.3B. It is trained in three stages (adaptors and image head; unified pretraining; supervised fine-tuning) with plain cross-entropy.
method.task: unified multimodal understanding (image-to-text) and text-to-image generation

datasets.name: ImageNet-1k
datasets.split: Stage I generation; Stage II only first 120K steps

datasets.name: Stage II mixture (text, interleaved WikiHow/WIT, captions, table/chart, generation)
datasets.size: generation data includes 2M in-house; other sizes not stated
datasets.source: DeepSeek-LLM text corpus; WikiHow [39]; WIT [72]; DeepSeek-VL table/chart [55]; various caption sets
datasets.preprocessing: captions as QA pairs; for [38,70] filtered by aesthetic score and image size leaving 20%; first sentence of caption used with 25% probability; gen format <caption><image>

datasets.name: Stage III instruction tuning mixture
datasets.size: generation includes 4M in-house; other sizes not stated
datasets.preprocessing: format 'User:<Input Message> \n Assistant: <Response>', loss on answers only

datasets.name: VQAv2, GQA, POPE, MME, SEED, MMBench, MM-Vet, MMMU

models.name: Janus
models.architecture: decoder-only autoregressive transformer with SigLIP understanding encoder, VQ generation encoder, MLP adaptors, text head and randomly initialised image head
models.tokenizer: LLM built-in tokenizer for text; VQ tokenizer from LlamaGen [73] for images

models.name: Semantic tokenizer (ablation only)
models.architecture: LlamaGen-style tokenizer with CNN encoder, VQ, extra 12-layer ViT semantic decoder (12 heads, hidden 768, causal mask) plus pixel decoder

models.name: Show-o, LWM, VILA-U, Chameleon, SDXL, DALL-E 2, LLaVA-v1.5 and others

training.objective: cross-entropy L = -sum log P(x_i|x_<i); loss on text tokens for understanding, on image tokens only for generation; no per-task loss weights
training.lr_schedule: Stage 1 cosine; Stage 2 constant; Stage 3 constant
training.regularisation: gradient clip 1.0 in all stages; text condition replaced by pad token with 10% probability for CFG

other.frozen: Stage I: encoders and LLM frozen, train understanding adaptor, generation adaptor, image head; Stage II: LLM unfrozen; Stage III: all but generation encoder fine-tuned
other.stage2_imagenet: ImageNet samples only in first 120K steps, other generation data in later 60K
other.semantic_tokenizer_training: 40 epochs ImageNet-1k then 1 epoch on 50 million images, constant lr 1e-4, batch 128, semantic loss weight 0.25 (BEiT-v2 cosine loss, SigLIP-Large-Patch16-384 teacher)
other.ablation_training_budget: not stated; whether ablation runs use the full schedule is unclear

inference.decoding: text: standard sampling from predicted distribution; image: next-token prediction with classifier-free guidance
inference.prompting: understanding data format as in Stage III chat template

metrics.name: MME-P, MMBench, SEED, VQAv2, GQA, MMMU, MM-Vet
FID on MSCOCO-30K / MJHQ-30K
metrics.definition: Frechet Inception Distance of generated images versus 30K high-quality images

metrics.name: GenEval overall
metrics.definition: instance-level compositional text-to-image benchmark (single obj, two obj, counting, colors, position, color attribute)

eval.protocol: Single reported numbers, no seeds, variance or significance tests stated; baseline numbers appear taken from other papers.

availability.data: in-house data (2M gen stage II, 4M gen stage III) not released as stated

results.claim: Janus 1.3B scores 87.0 on POPE, 69.4 MMBench and 63.7 SEED, above LLaVA-v1.5 7B and Qwen-VL-Chat 7B.
results.setup: Janus 1.3B, final model after 3 stages, Table 2
results.quote: Janus (1.3B) achieved scores of 69.4, 63.7, and 87.0, respectively, outperforming LLaVA-v1.5 (7B) [50] and Qwen-VL-Chat (7B) [3]
results.note: Paper text lists MMBench, SEED, POPE; Qwen-VL-Chat has no POPE entry in Table 2.

results.claim: Ablation: a single VQ tokenizer for both understanding and generation (Exp-A) drops POPE to 60.1 versus 87.0 for decoupled SigLIP + VQ (Exp-D).
results.setup: Table 5 ablation, 1.3B Janus architecture, Exp-A shared VQ tokenizer trained on Und.+Gen. versus Exp-D SigLIP+VQ Und.+Gen.; ablation training schedule not stated
results.table: Table 5, row A (VQ Tokenizer, Und. + Gen.), column POPE 60.1; row D 87.0
results.note: Exp-A MMB 35.0, SEED 34.9, MMMU 24.7, COCO-FID 8.72; Exp-D MMB 69.4, SEED 63.7, MMMU 30.5, FID 8.53.

results.claim: A stronger semantic tokenizer (Exp-B) with a shared encoder gets POPE 82.4 and COCO-FID 7.11, still below decoupled on understanding but better on FID.
results.setup: Table 5 row B, SigLIP-distilled semantic tokenizer, Und.+Gen.
results.table: Table 5, row B (SE. Tokenizer, Und. + Gen.), column POPE 82.4
results.note: COCO-FID 7.11 for B versus 8.53 for D; authors hypothesise more coherent semantic IDs and a much larger encoder.

results.claim: Training the semantic-tokenizer model on understanding only (Exp-C) beats the shared Und.+Gen. version (Exp-B) on understanding, which the authors read as a trade-off in a single encoder.
results.setup: Table 5 row C vs row B
results.table: Table 5, row C (SE. Tokenizer, Und.), column POPE 83.9

results.claim: Unified training of decoupled Janus is comparable to understanding-only or generation-only training.
results.setup: Table 5 rows D vs E (POPE 87.0 vs 85.9, MMB 69.4 vs 70.6) and D vs F (FID 8.53 vs 8.92)
results.quote: Experimental results show that the performance of unified training is comparable to that of training solely for understanding or solely for visual generation.

results.claim: Janus gets 61% overall on GenEval, above Show-o (53%), SDXL (55%) and DALL-E 2 (52%).
results.setup: Janus 1.3B, 384x384 output, CFG scale 5; baseline numbers as printed in Table 3
results.quote: our Janus obtains 61% overall accuracy on GenEval, which outperforms the previous best unified model Show-o (53%) and some popular generation-only methods, e.g., SDXL (55%) and DALL-E 2 (52%)
results.note: Position 0.46 and color attribute 0.42 are Janus's strongest gains over Show-o (0.11, 0.28); counting 0.30 is lower than Show-o 0.49.

results.claim: Janus FID is 8.53 on COCO-30K and 10.10 on MJHQ-30K.
results.setup: Janus 1.3B, CFG 5; baseline Show-o 9.24 on COCO-30K, 15.18 on MJHQ-30K
results.quote: Janus achieves FIDs of 8.53 and 10.10 on the COCO-30K and MJHQ-30K benchmarks, respectively
results.note: VILA-U (384) has 7.69 on MJHQ-30K, better than Janus 10.10; PixArt-alpha 7.32 on COCO-30K also better.

results.claim: Janus improves MME from 949 to 1338 (41%) and GQA from 48.7 to 59.1 (30%) over Show-o.
results.quote: we achieve performance improvements of 41% (949 →1338) and 30% (48.7 →59.1) on the MME and GQA datasets, respectively
results.note: Table 2 prints Show-o MME-P as 948.4, text prints 949.

results.claim: Full training took 7 days on 16 nodes of 8 A100 40GB GPUs.
results.quote: The whole training process took 7 days on a cluster of 16 nodes, each equipped with 8 Nvidia A100 (40GB) GPUs.

results.claim: Janus applies classifier-free guidance to logits with default scale 5; text condition was dropped with 10% probability in training.
results.setup: Image generation inference, l_g = l_u + s(l_c - l_u)
results.quote: The default number of 𝑠is 5 for the following evaluation.

results.claim: Despite English-only text-to-image training data, Janus generates from prompts in other languages.
results.quote: despite our training data consisting solely of English text-to-image data, Janus can still process text-to-image tasks in other languages

limits: Only 384x384 resolution; Fig 4 compares against SDXL at 1024 and LlamaGen at 512.
Ablation training budgets and sizes are not stated; each ablation is a single run with no variance.
Baseline numbers are taken from other papers; training and in-house data are not released.
Semantic tokenizer used only in ablation; Exp-B beats Janus on FID, which the authors attribute to semantic IDs and a larger encoder (hypothesis, untested).
Understanding benchmarks lag larger models on several columns (e.g. LLaVA-v1.5 7B has higher MME-P 1510.7, GQA 62.0, VQAv2 78.5).
Qualitative meme comparisons are cherry-picked examples, no systematic evaluation.
No limitations section; authors list possible extensions (stronger encoders, higher resolution, diffusion loss, more modalities) but do not test them.

lineage.note: Single VQ tokenizer for both tasks; Janus ablation Exp-A follows this and shows poor understanding
lineage.quote: Following previous work [77], we select a VQ tokenizer [73] to encode images for both multimodal understanding and generation tasks, serving as the baseline (Exp-A).
